title: French Magazine Lampooned Religious, Political Figures

image.attribution: Joachim Roncin, Charlie Hebdo / Wikimedia Commons / CC0

main_content:
The French satirical weekly newspaper Charlie Hebdohad just tweeted a cartoon mocking Islamic State group leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi when masked gunmen burst into its Paris office Wednesday.

Paris police said at least 12 people were killed, including two police officers, and at least 11 others were injured, with four listed in critical condition.

Ten members of the Charlie Hebdo staff died in the attack, prosecutors said. Among the dead were three cartoonists, including co-founder Jean “Cabu” Cabut and editor-in-chief Stephane “Charb” Charbonnier.

Charlie Hebdo, which publishes every Wednesday, is known for being irreverent, anti-establishment and virulently anti-religious.

But its attacks on Muslims have caused the most controversy, including a court case on charges of racism and the firebombing of its offices in 2011 after the Sharia Hebdo edition. “Hebdo” is French slang for a weekly newspaper.

The weekly has had permanent police protection since the firebombing incident.

“Extremists don’t need any excuses,” Charbonnier said following the firebombing of his magazine offices, in which no one was hurt. “If they are not amused by our cartoons, they don’t need to buy our magazine. Of course they are allowed to demonstrate. The right to protest needs to be protected, so long as one abides by the law and refrains from violence.”

Minutes before the attack Wednesday, Charlie Hebdo had tweeted a satirical cartoon of the extremist Islamic State group’s leader with a New Year’s message that read: “Best wishes, by the way.”

The extremist leader has previously urged his followers to attack citizens of the U.S., France and other countries involved in an international coalition, whose goal is to destroy the Islamic State group.

questions.question: What happened minutes after the satirical weekly tweeted a cartoon mocking the Islamic State?
options: Masked gunmen burst into the Paris office and opened fire.
The cartoon received widespread international acclaim.
Police began an investigation into the magazine's activities.
A large protest erupted outside their office.
questions.answer: Masked gunmen burst into the Paris office and opened fire.

questions.question: How many people were seriously injured in the attack?
options: More than 20 were injured, with at least 10 in critical condition.
At least 11 others were injured, with four listed in critical condition.
Only three individuals were seriously injured during the attack.
The police reported no serious injuries among the staff.
questions.answer: At least 11 others were injured, with four listed in critical condition.

questions.question: Which high-profile members of the magazine were killed in the attack?
options: Jean “Cabu” Cabut and Stephane “Charb” Charbonnier were among the casualties.
The entire editorial board was killed in the incident.
The founder of the magazine was injured but survived.
Only police officers were killed during the attack.
questions.answer: Jean “Cabu” Cabut and Stephane “Charb” Charbonnier were among the casualties.
